| [QUESTION-120](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-120.md) v4 | When the record meets a random linear map that keeps what a later stage needs, in random features for kernels, the compressed-sensing bound on superposition, and the expand-and-threshold codes of sparse distributed memory and the fly, is it one concentration-of-measure fact applied to different families, and does each threshold count the same thing? | Filed when a survey of the record found random projections in three places and the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma in none. The question is whether these are one union bound over different families or different phenomena that share a tool. Six anchor works are now read.
